name: Electoral Reform Society
summary: A UK campaigning organisation, founded in 1884, that works for proportional representation for the House of Commons and for other changes to how the UK votes and is governed: an elected House of Lords, votes at 16, fairer voting for mayors and councils. It has offices in London, Edinburgh (ERS Scotland) and Cardiff (ERS Cymru), about 7,000 members and 18 staff. It is a company limited by guarantee owned by its members, not a registered charity, so gifts to it get no Gift Aid or tax relief; most of its spending is drawn from a £43 million capital fund built from the 2018 sale of its former ballot-services business. It spent £2.4 million in the year to March 2025.

spending.source: https://electoral-reform.org.uk/latest-news-and-research/publications/annual-review-2025-our-year-campaigning-for-change/ (Annual Review 2025, finances for the year to 31 March 2025: campaign and research staff in England £686,153, Scotland £207,101 and Wales £267,852, and campaigns, communications, members and events £418,971, together £1,580,077 at $1.277 per pound, of total expenditure of £2,370,778; the audited accounts for the years to March 2025 and 2026 are filed without the income and expenditure account)

lines.label: Campaigns and research for proportional representation and UK democratic reform (England, Scotland and Wales)
lines.source: https://electoral-reform.org.uk/latest-news-and-research/publications/annual-review-2025-our-year-campaigning-for-change/ (Annual Review 2025, expenditure 2024-25): the campaign staff in three nations and the campaigns' own costs, £1,580,077; one model covers them as six branches (proportional representation, the supplementary vote, votes at 16, the devolved franchise acts, the hereditary peers, the Senedd).
